TextEng: This burly fellow looks stressed at having to manage such an overcrowded inn. He barely glances at you as he speaks. "What d'you want, stranger?"
The innkeeper turns away without another word.
"Short and sweet. Choose your poison, then."
"So would a dozen others. Fact is, every single room in the inn is taken. I'd be piling them into my own room if I could, but the wife is so ugly she'd scare them off. You'll need to look elsewhere."
"Yeah? Look around, squire. The place is heaving. Every moment I waste standing around answering your inane questions is one more complaint from a patron. Take it elsewhere."
"Aye, that right? One of the Bron's deputies marched him down the stairs and out the door but a short time ago. Said a day or two in the stocks would teach him a lesson."
"Farewell."
"I want a drink."
<StartAction>[Leave.]</Start>
<StartAction>[Start merchant.]</Start>
"I'd like to rent a room."
"I have some questions."
"I'm looking for Lashan Waters."
This silver-haired half-elf is a rare beauty. Like a dark shadow passing under the surface of a moonlit lake, a deep sadness mars her otherwise perfect features.
"Greetings to you. I am Alamarayne, high priestess of the Temple of the Half-moon. I am sorry if you find me less loquacious than usual. There has been a great tragedy here."
"A tentacle...? Eremuth - he is here! It must be him."
"I see you have some idea of who the killer may be. I pray you find him or her quickly - before they kill again."
"I cannot begin to think who could be responsible for such a terrible crime. Something inhuman for certain."
"Someone very dear to me was murdered. It is best you speak with Thoyana about it - the investigation is still ongoing. I believe she is at the docks."
"Welcome back to our temple. How may the servants of Selûne assist you?"
"Someone very dear to me was murdered. It is best you speak with Thoyana about it - the investigation is still ongoing. I believe she is at the docks."
"Thank the Moonmaiden you arrived to hunt down Elenawen's killer. Without you, I fear that creature would have killed many others."
"May the silver light of Selûne guide you."
"As high priestess of the Moonmaiden, it is my sworn duty to heal those in need. I will summon the power of my goddess to cleanse your wounds."
"It is done. How else may I assist you?"
"We do not keep much here, for this temple is but a modest one. Still, you are welcome to purchase what we do have in stock."
"Selûne is the goddess of the moon and one of the most ancient of Faerûn's deities. She shares the secrets of the night that her dark twin Shar would see hidden in order to bring mortals to ruin."

"Yes. I was saying my final prayer of the night to Our Lady of Silver when by Her light, I spotted Elenawen's body crumpled by the temple wall. I sent word to Thoyana and laid the poor girl to rest in the catacombs below."
"Certainly."
"The poor girl's throat was torn out. It was as though some kind of probe or tentacle buried itself in her neck and ripped it open. I am sorry; the memory of it upsets me still."
"Farewell."
"Let's talk about something else."
"Anything else you can tell me? How did she die?"
"Do you have any idea who is responsible?"
"What do you mean?"
"Tell me about this tragedy."
"You mentioned a tragedy."
"I am in need of healing."
"I want to see your temple goods."
<StartAction>[Leave.]</Start>
<StartAction>[Start merchant.]</Start>
"Tell me about Selûne."
"Thoyana told me that you found Elenawen's body."
"That wyvern almost had you, Tyrian. You're getting old."
"Speak for yourself! You'd be less fleet of foot too if you had to carry this horn around everywhere we go!"
"Not that pompous fool Red Nazala? You realize that spelling your name backwards doesn't fool ANYONE?"
"Ahem. Where were we? Ah, yes. What may we do for you, Hero of Tethyr?"
"Ah, now this is a little embarrassing. I told you it was a bad idea to call ourselves the Dukes of Daggerford, Tyrian. We were hardly involved in that whole fiasco."

"Speak for yourself! You showed up once all the hard work had already been done! Anyway, it's a pleasure to meet the true hero of Daggerford. Oh, we killed a few orcs, took out a few Zhents, that kind of thing. But without you, it would all have been in vain."
"Our bard, Codepoetz, even composed a song about your deeds."
"I BEGAN to compose a song. One day, I may even finish it - if I ever get a moment's respite from cleaning up your two's messes!"
"Ahem. Where were we? Ah, yes. What may we do for you, Hero of Daggerford?"
"Well met again. What may the Dukes do for you?"
"We have indeed. We made it all the way to the Kur-Tharsu citadel before we had to turn back. Thar is an extremely dangerous place. We failed to prepare and paid the price."
"Let me mark the Scarred Lands on your map. From there, you must pass through a noxious marshland before arriving at the gates of Kur-Tharsu."
"Gentlemen, we have guests."

"If you are determined to investigate Kur-Tharsu, you will need every ally you can get - as well as horses - or it is unlikely you will make it very far. Thar is a deadly place. Even the Hero of Neverwinter would be tested."
"Whatever happened to the Hero of Neverwinter? They seemed to fade from history."
"History has a way of revealing many truths if only one looks hard enough. Now, friend, was there anything else you required?"
"Certainly."
"I think not. Our time here in the Moonsea is at an end. We planned for this moment for thirteen years, and it is bittersweet to have fallen short at the end. But such is life."

"Reaching the Scarred Lands leading to Kur-Tharsu requires horses - unless you wish to be harassed by humanoids every step of the way. The citadel gate is mighty and can only be breached by powerful magic or, perhaps, a siege weapon of some kind."
"Alas, we forgot to buy horses, and by the time we reached the Scarred Lands, our magic was spent from countless encounters. We had no means of entering the citadel."
"The ogre citadel is ancient. Rumors say it was once the stronghold of the Tharkul, an ogre king who united all the beast-men of Thar, as the ogres once called themselves."

"We were not able to breach its gates. Giants, wyverns, and worse serve the ogre mages within. There is even a rumor that the ancient black dragon Iyrauroth has returned to the area, though, fortunately, we did not encounter him."

"I know of no mage by that name. However, the ogres of Kur-Tharsu have a mysterious new ally they call the Raven Mage. We glimpsed him once; he has but one eye and wears a long, dark coat. I imagine he is within, with the ogre mages."
"Well met, friend. We are the Dukes. You look familiar. Did you serve alongside the Crimson Guard down in Tethyr? Or was it that business down in Daggerford?"
"Then please excuse me. My mistake. What may we do for you?"
"May Ao guide you to the truth."
"Whatever it is adventuring groups usually do. Exploring, pestering the locals, heroing. Is that even a word? Heroing?"
"You tell me. You're supposedly the wordsmith among us."
"Right. Anyway, suffice it to say that after that business down south in Calimshan, Tethyr, Daggerford, and now Thar, we're due a city break. Westgate is apparently nice this time of year..."
"That's right! I recall I was in Darromar at the time. We might have met once, now that I think about it. I was possibly going under a different guise."
"I am the Hero of Daggerford. I defeated the devil Gorgomorz."
"Ulblyn Blackalbuck told me you've just returned from Thar."
"Thank you for the information."
"I want to discuss Thar again."
"You mentioned you failed to prepare."
"I am heading there soon. You could join me."
"What do you mean you failed to prepare?"
"Tell me more of Kur-Tharsu."
"I'm looking for an archmage named Maganus."
"I have no idea what you're talking about."
"Farewell."
"What are you doing in Melvaunt?"
"I served in Tethyr. I helped turn the crimson tides in our favor."

This half-elf appears no older than thirty, although you suspect her true age is close to twice that. She has the lean, muscular frame one would expect of an ex-adventurer of no small stature. Her voice is cold and business-like.

"Well met. I am Amaril Sweetwater, and this is the Gold Cave. Don't let the name fool you; there's no gold ore to be found here. Rather, this is the largest center of trade in Elventree. I stock all the adventuring gear one could possibly need."
"I'm always open for business."
"Take a good look. You won't find a better selection of goods in Elventree."
"Too much talk is bad for business. If you need information, I suggest speaking with Hilrad the Patient or some other elder of the village."
"Hello again. What do you need?"
"Farewell."
"Let me see your merchandise."
<StartAction>[Leave.]</Start>
<StartAction>[Start merchant.]</Start>
"I want to ask some questions."

"Honored guests! Friends and allies! Nay, family! The ceremony will now begin! First, it is my great pleasure to welcome Tharchion Dmitra Flass of Thay and High Blade Selfaril Uoumdolphin of Mulmaster. Their love is what truly brings us together here."
"Greetings, Ambassador."
"Leave me be."
"The honor is ours."

"Gods, but what a sight to behold! Sune herself has blessed the pair of you! On behalf of the Zulkirs of Thay, I offer our warmest greetings. In recognition of the upcoming anniversary of your blessed union and our unbreakable alliance, they offer this gift."

"A dozen gem golems, each worth a small fortune! Many slaves died to mine the gems necessary for the creation of these wondrous constructs - but who can put a price on the celebration of true love, I ask you?"

"Beautiful though they are, the true value of these golems lies in their formidable combat prowess. When commanded, they will attack your foes with unbridled rage. Few could hope to overcome a single golem. None may stand against twelve!"
"This is indeed a generous gift, Ambassador. You have my thanks."
"Mine also. Please relay our appreciation to-- Wait. What is happening?"
"Forgive me, they... they should not have activated. I did not give the command. Stop! What-- what are you doing?"
"Treachery! Protect the Tharchion and the High Blade!"
"Curse my lack-witted husband! What possessed me to have married such a buffoon? My mother was right about him all along. He's a good-for-nothing unfit for the hand of a Goldwaters!"
"Yes, begone and leave us to our dilemma."

"I don't know what happened to the man I once loved. It feels like the Cheswick I married died long ago. I know he has done you wrong, but I beg you, do him no harm until we've had the chance to speak with him."
"Don't leave me here alone, I beg you!"
"Please, let us leave this dreadful place and speak with my husband first. I'll answer your questions after."
"Can we leave now?"
"Where is my husband?"
"My thanks to you."
"Bah! Go and pester my husband. He is more suited to converse with the common rabble than I."
"Speak with my husband. It's his fault we are in this pickle."
"I am the honorable lady Amberlyn Goldwaters, heiress of the esteemed Goldwaters merchant family of Sembia. This pig of a man is my husband, I am sorry to say."
Amberlyn is filthy and bruised, her elegant gown torn and covered in grime. The arrogance and bluster seems to have been stripped away; she looks like a broken woman. Her voice is a hoarse whisper.
"It's you... Gods, I never would have believed you would rescue me. Cheswick was sure the frost giants would tear you apart."
"I have no gold. Even my clothes are ruined. When I return to Sembia, I will arrange for a handsome reward to be sent. But I can't return! Cheswick..."
"Cheswick! He bribed the leader of the giants - offered my life and the promise to send more victims their way if they let him walk free."
"He was SMILING as the giants carried me away! I'll never forget the evil look in his eyes. He said he would send you after me - that he wanted you 'out of the way.' "
"Farewell."
"I like his style. I'd do the same in his situation."
"Perhaps it was a ruse to buy time to rescue you."
"That heartless scoundrel! How could he?"
"That's it. Now he's a dead man."
"We need to speak with your husband."
"Wait here for the moment."
"I want to ask some questions."
<StartAction>[Take Amberlyn back to Ogson's caravan.]</Start>
"That's quite an attitude you have."
"Tell me what the problem is."
"Who are you?"
"Bah, I eat giants for breakfast."
"I believe I'm due a hefty sum of gold for this."
"What do you mean?"
"Sorry, can't talk now. I need to get this wheel fixed."
"Welcome again. How may I help?"
"Here are your new mounts. Please treat them with respect and compassion. In return, they will prove as loyal as any hound."
"I am terribly sorry, but I don't have any horses available right now. However, I am soon to take delivery of a trio of magnificent war horses. Return shortly, and I hope to have them available."
"Certainly. As it happens, you are in luck. I recently acquired three of the finest young war horses from a Sembian trader. I am willing to sell them as a package deal for 1,500 gold pieces."
"As you wish. What else do you need?"

"Excellent! If you will accompany me to the stables, I'll ready your new mounts..." <StartHighlight>[For instructions on how to use mounts, please check the "Expedition to Thar: Mounts" entry in your journal.]</Start>

"I fear this particular breed does not enjoy being separated from its fellows. If you wish to come back in the summer, I should have them trained enough to sell separately. Until then, I'm afraid I can only sell as a package."
"I assure you, stranger, my reputation as both a ranger and a trader in horseflesh is everything to me. I would not sell you a lame horse, as much out of empathy for the horse as for you."
"Hail there, adventurer. I am Angrym, and this is my livery stable. I have devoted my life to understanding and mastering every beast a man or woman could wish to ride. How may I assist you?"
"A pleasure doing business with you."
"Very well. My days are spent among animals and beasts, so a little conversation is welcome now and then."

"Not that I know of, but they sometimes pass through here. This city has no issue with Harpers. In return, they find little reason to visit. Thentia is a free and fair place compared with the likes of Zhentil Keep or Melvaunt."
"An archmage? Thentia is home to several. The closest and friendliest to outsiders is Flammuldinath, known locally as Firefingers. His tower is in the north of the city."

"It's funny you ask. A group of Shadovar arrived in the nearby ruins recently. They are searching for some kind of artifact. I hope they find what they are looking for and leave before Firefingers and the others get involved."

"Ha, I see you've heard the rumors about me! I'm afraid my stables are a little sparse this time of year. I have a great many rothé, of course, but such beasts require weeks of training to ride effectively."

"In the past, I have stabled pegasi, griffins, even a unicorn or two. Return in the summer, and I hope to have a more exotic assortment of animals to present to you. Please note, I only sell such marvels to responsible owners!"
"Farewell."
"I need to buy horses."
"Forget it."
"I'll take them."
"Can't I just buy one?"
"This had better not be a scam!"
"I just have some questions."
"Let me ask something else."
"Are there any Harpers active in Thentia?"
"Do you know where I can find an archmage?"
"Anything of note happening around here?"
"Do you have anything more exotic?"
Blizzard lies stricken on the blood-soaked earth, her robes in tatters. Despite the burns covering her body, she still appears to be breathing.
"Once again, the foul spy <FirstName> has emerged victorious from a desperate struggle!"
"Alas, Blizzard was not so fortunate. Look upon her, ladies and gentlemen: her flesh seared, the clothes ripped from her back. A sad end to an illustrious career."
The crowd gasps as the announcer continues. "All that remains is for <FirstName> to deliver the coup de grâce! Out with the old, in with the new! Well, <FirstName>? Deal the fatal blow!"

The crowd goes momentarily silent as you strike the fatal blow and then bursts into cheers. Chants of '<FirstName>' echo around the Arena. The announcer raises his hands. "And so we have a new champion! You are witnessing the birth of a legend!"

The crowd goes quiet, then erupts into a chorus of sniggers and claps. The announcer looks confused for a moment and then smiles. "Spoken like the black-hearted fiend <he/she> is! Very well, Blizzard is given a temporary stay of execution."

The crowd gasps as one, and you see a lot of angry faces staring down at you. The announcer shakes his head in disgust. "It would seem <FirstName> is a coward in addition to <his/her> other failings. So be it. They shall be taken back to their cell."
<StartAction>[Strike the death blow.]</Start>
<StartAction>[Bluff]</Start> "I won't sully my hands by striking this dog!"
"I will not commit this evil deed!"

The gray eyes of this slender swordsman pass dismissively over the corpses of the slaadi at his feet. Despite the whirlwind of cold steel he unleashed but a moment ago, his breathing is steady. He regards you coolly as you approach.
"These slaadi grow more numerous by the day. You must have a death wish to be traveling these roads - at least without an army to back you up."
"You're welcome to try, assassin. I've been waiting for this moment a long time."

"I was once a Blade, one of the ruling nobles of Mulmaster, and the only one not a puppet of Selfaril. He ordered me to eliminate a city official, a young woman. I refused and was banished from the city. The High Blade has never forgiven me."

A look of distaste shows on the assassin's face. "The High Blade displays surprising cowardice for a warrior of his reputation. Perhaps once I am finished with you, I will teach him a lesson. Now I must collect your bounty. Rest assured, it is nothing personal."
"Continue east. Hillsfar is not far from here."
The swordsman's eyes flicker briefly with interest. "Grazkahn. One of the slaadi I fought on my way here squealed the name over and over, thinking to cow me. My sword silenced it soon enough."
"I suspect he must be somewhere close if the numbers of slaadi in the region are any indication. Such a being is surely powerful."

"You are either foolish or supremely confident. The latter is not a fault provided one can match words with deeds. Regardless, Grazkahn is your problem." The swordsman's eyes flicker to Astar. "He's mine."
"Are we finished here? I grow impatient."
"You return. Why do you bother me once more?"
"Leave me. I must continue the hunt for the one I seek."
"You are free to leave. Astar Graysteel, however, is a different matter."
"You had your chance. Artemis Entreri is no sage. However, I understand Shadowdale is home to the most famous sage of all. March hard, and you will make it there within a tenday."
"You are free to leave. Astar Graysteel, however, is a different matter."
Dead-gray eyes lock with icy blue. Astar's face is like a mask carved from stone. "So, Selfaril finally sent you after me. I should be pleased he hired the best."
The assassin shrugs. "He is paying well, and he promised it would be a challenge. I would never have accepted unless both those conditions were met. The High Blade of Mulmaster wants you dead."

Before you is a man of advanced years who nonetheless stands as straight as an arrow. Despite his impressive bearing, there is something disquieting about him - as though there is more than meets the eye...

"Arr. Ye must be the Hero of the Moonsea, as I've heard some of me captains refer to ye. Tell me, how did ye fare in your voyage to Kur-Tharsu? Did ye find what ye were looking for? A sword, mayhaps?"

Avagard grins, revealing brown teeth, and his ancient face crinkles in mirth. It is not his teeth that grab your attention, however. It is his eyes - pale and milky with age but with an unmistakable gold glimmer...

"Arr. Or should I say, 'ah.' I see understanding finally dawns. Our little tale takes another twist, does it not? While you were off chasing Maganus and the fake sword I so carefully planted, I was using the real Dominion to raise an army."

"I have to confess, I never expected that crazy bastard to summon Orcus. I underestimated him. I did not underestimate YOU, however. Hence why you are now surrounded by pirates bent to my will. Meet my captains - you may be familiar with them."
"I'm sorry... I cannot resist... the sword's pull..."

"It amused me to take the guise of this salty old sea dog. In reality, Avagard died years ago. I believe his heart failed him. A less than poetic end, but oddly fitting for one of his disappointing species."

"I must take my leave now. It is possible you will survive even this, of course - but know that if you do, we will not meet again. The malaugrym can travel places mere mortals cannot. It's been delightful catching up. Say hello to Astar in the afterlife."

"I must take my leave now. Excellent work slaying my sister and the hapless agents of the Unseen, by the way. They were a hindrance to my plans. Once again, you danced to my tune like the puppet you are. Farewell, puppet."
"There is something odd about you."
"What is going on here?"
"How do you know about that?"

"Well? Have you made a decision?"

"Fzoul Chembryl. Chosen of Bane and High Lord of the Zhentarim. I have waited a long time for this moment."
"<FirstName>! This... this is a betrayal I would never have expected of you. Why do so much good only to turn around and throw your lot in with this tyrant? I am devastated."
"Fear not, Harper. Your disappointment will be brief. Apprehend her - she will hang immediately after this wizard twitches his last."
"Then you are an ungrateful fool. I could have granted you power beyond your wildest dreams. As gratitude for your help, I will let your arrogance slide this once. You may show yourself out."
"Pah! Do you have mud between your ears? This wizard's guilt is beyond question. Do not think to stand in the way of Zhentarim justice, or you will join this wizard on the gallows."
"Why are you damned 'heroes' so impossible?! Have it your way - this temple shall become your grave!"
"Begone from this temple."

"Excellent! I have a feeling you and I shall enjoy a long and prosperous partnership. First, we shall give this troublemaker the death he so richly deserves - and then we shall make plans to expand the Zhentarim's power!"
"Why are you damned 'heroes' so impossible?! Have it your way - this temple shall become your grave!"
"M-mighty Bane... as your Chosen, I beg you - aid us! We cannot achieve victory without you!"
"Bane is coming - I can sense him. We need to get out of here. No mortal may stand before a god of such power, especially in their own temple. Follow me."
"You summoned this demon? Imbecile! Do you know nothing? Orcus cannot be controlled! You may have doomed us all!"

"Fzoul is right. This is madness."
"Orcus must be stopped. He will destroy the entire city"
"You fought well, <class>."
"The demon army is defeated, and the Zhentarim will grow stronger still!"
"I hope I am granted the honor of executing that traitorous wizard."

"The Dark Lord triumphs again!"
"I have truly never seen an uglier collection of demons than that rabble."

"This is the only way to live!"

"I heard someone won big last night."
"I'm feeling lucky."

Father Garth is so badly wounded it's a wonder he's still standing. His left hip has been shattered, and blood soaks the ground where he stands. His right arm is hanging on by a thread; the minotaur's axe has almost taken it off.

Despite his grievous injuries, Father Garth's expression is serene. Although his voice is still clear, you can see that his eyes are clouding over. "<FirstName>... you're still alive. I... had feared you dead."

The last of his strength spent, the old man tumbles to the ground. He is dead before his body settles onto the bloodstained earth. The crowd goes silent for a moment - and then a roar erupts as the Red Minotaur charges towards you.
"So tired. I must rest..."
Father Garth is in a terrible state, his lips swollen and his face a mass of bruises. He attempts a gap-toothed smile as you approach.
"It's good to see you looking so well, my friend. I passed the driders on the way here. Truly vicious creatures."

"It is unusual for such dangerous monsters to be matched against a newcomer. Most start out battling other gladiators - perhaps a goblin or wolf. The Innovator of Pain must consider you powerful indeed."

"Thank you for your compassion, but I will survive. The Innovator of Pain will make certain of it. I take solace in the fact that I am an old man and not long for this world. No priestly magic can undo death by natural causes."

Father Garth coughs - a hacking, breathless sound - and blood stains his lips. "It will be a while before I am called to the fighting pit again. I will use this opportunity to pray to Ilmater for an end to the suffering in this place."
"I must persevere. In this place, all that exists is pain and suffering. I believe I was put here for a reason: that Ilmater sent me here to test me."
"The Innovator summoned her a short time ago. I fear something terrible awaits her in the Arena; her cold efficiency has made her unpopular with the patrons. They wish her dead."
"Callous words, <FirstName>. That attitude may be the best way to survive in this fell place, but take care not to lose your soul along the way."
The old priest gazes sadly at the fallen orc. "Elf fought valiantly. He even put a nick or two in the minotaur's flesh. The monster shrugs off wounds like they aren't there."
"I don't believe so. You are still new, fresh, exciting. When the crowd chants for your blood, it is part of the game. With Blizzard, I fear they have lost interest. That is fatal in the Arena."
"Aye, I shall pray for her. In the four years we have been here together, I have learned little of her, but I know in my heart that, despite her anger, she is a good woman."

The priest's face breaks into a kindly smile. "Ilmater is the god of endurance, perseverance, and self-sacrifice. Everyone must suffer at some point in their life. The followers of Ilmater seek to lessen that burden. A burden shared is a burden halved."

"I was born in Mulmaster - to a noble family of great wealth. The Aumantor clan was proud and haughty but lacking humility and compassion. I was the second son of Marcus Aumantor. He was a greedy man who dabbled in slavery."
"My father double-crossed an unscrupulous slaver and was assassinated. With my father gone, the family fell to ruin. I took what I could and fled."
As the priest bids you farewell, the door to the cell opens, and the sinister voice of the Innovator of Pain softly calls out your name.
"He expects you to fight again so soon? Here - allow me to aid you. I will call upon Ilmater's power to heal you."
Father Garth sags forward, his face ashen. "K-keep your... chin up. I must rest."
"Certainly."
"They were like a pack of jackals, all trying to grab more than their share of the family's wealth. My mother had long since passed. I could not remain among my kin."
"While Elf and the Red Minotaur fought, I refused to attack the beast. Still, Elf fought to protect me. Perhaps I can save his life before I die."

"With nowhere to go and sick of the infighting between my relatives, I spent the next few months staying in the various inns of the city. One night, I was set upon by a gang of ruffians. They recognized me - and they hated my family."
"I would have died but for the intervention of another guest. He took a terrible beating on my behalf. That man was a slave in my household for fifteen years. And yet he saved my life."
"He was a priest of Ilmater. When my family could no longer afford to keep slaves, he was cast out onto the street. He set me on the path to finding myself in Ilmater's service."

The old priest nods. "He was. When my family could no longer afford to keep slaves and he was freed, he dedicated himself to spreading the word of Ilmater. His actions forced me to reevaluate my life. Soon after, I chose the path of Ilmater."
"Eight years back, I was apprehended while visiting a shrine to Ilmater here in Hillsfar. The Red Plume who arrested me was yet another former slave of my family."
"He arranged to have me thrown into the Arena. I've been here since."
"Hello again! Speak with Elf and Blizzard. They shall tell you more of this place. I must meditate and seek guidance from my god."

This old man wears ragged brown robes that are torn and covered in grime. His weathered face is covered in scars that do nothing to diminish his kindly smile. His blue eyes are still sharp despite the years, and his voice is strong.
"Ah, you're finally awake. You were out for several hours; someone gave you quite the bash on the head. I am Father Garth, devout servant of Ilmater."
The old man inclines his head. "Forgive my curiosity, but I couldn't help but overhear Officer Onehand's discussion with the Innovator after you were brought here. You possess quite the reputation."

" I am old, and death for me is a welcome release. You must conserve your power for the battle against the minotaur. Let nature take its course. But Elf... I have the power to heal him, although it will drain the last vestiges of my strength."

"Onehand said you were a Harper ally and should be under close supervision at all times. The Innovator will be keen to break you."
"In the eight years I have been here, only one gladiator has ever gained freedom from this place. Lord Maalthiir granted the Red Minotaur its freedom."

"Speak with Elf and Blizzard. Relish the peace and tranquility while you can. Soon you will be called upon to enter the fighting pit. We will talk later."

"The walls of this complex are enchanted so that no teleportation magic will function within. The golems are all but impervious to magic and physical harm. Many have tried to escape, my friend. They all perished."

"The wizard over there is Blizzard. She's been here for years. For such a young woman, she possesses unusual power. She suffers - of that I have no doubt - but she is unwilling to share her burden with me. Perhaps she never will. It gives her strength."

"The orc is a recent arrival. He's a strange one, exhibiting the mannerisms and speech of an elf despite all evidence to the contrary. Blizzard believes the poor creature suffers from a sickness of the mind, but I'm not so sure. Perhaps you should speak with him to learn more."
"The Innovator of Pain. It is a title the arena master has adopted. The name is apt. He is a madman who revels in the suffering of his gladiators."

He looks at you with fading eyes. "I offer you a choice, <FirstName>. With my remaining power, I can call upon my god to grant you the strength to defeat the minotaur. If I do this, Elf will die, but you will likely be able to defeat the beast."
"I gather you ran afoul of Wak Rathar, Maalthiir's closest friend. Wak has free reign to terrorize Hillsfar's populace and is actively encouraged by Maalthiir to keep these cells well stocked."
"We are in the bowels of Lord Maalthiir's arena. Above us is the fighting pit. This cell is but one of many that make up this underground complex."

"My full name is Gareth Aumantor. The name is a haughty one, noble and yet unworthy. When I chose to discard my material possessions in the service of Ilmater, I cast it off. Now I am known simply as Father Garth."

"If I heal Elf, you will be able to fight the minotaur together. He is a skilled warrior, but he may not make as much difference as my god's power would when invested in you. But you may both yet survive."
"With the last of my strength, I shall bring Elf back from the brink of death. The blessings of Ilmater go with you. May you one day escape this place and tell the stories of those that died here."

"Tell me how I escape."

"Where am I?"

"Woo hoo! Free at last from that dratted bottle! How long has it been? A tenday? A month? Hang on - this isn't Calimshan! Where is this? What YEAR is this?"

"Before I go, you're entitled to a single wish. You probably know the score by now: word it properly or it will backfire, etc. Truth be told, I can't be bothered to get creative, so do us both a favor and wish for something reasonable, yes?"
"FINE! Too good for to ask a wish of this humble genie, are you? No skin off my nose, no siree!

"Your wish is my command! Spoiler: it's not Elminster. I'm sorry to disappoint."
"Oh, bless you! It looks like you're already on one, but I like your face, so I'm grant you a little extra experience to help with whatever adventures come your way!"
"My, I've never heard THAT one before! Take this ring. It should provide what you wished for. More or less."
"OF COURSE you do. Who doesn't? 5,000 gold pieces, coming right up!"
"Now then, I'm off south - this place is grimmer than a box full of turds! Be well, mortal!"
"Never mind that. Where's my reward?"
"We're in Melvaunt. It's 1373 DR."
"I wish for extreme power."
"I wish to be incredibly wealthy."
"I don't want a wish."
"I wish for unlimited wishes!"
"I wish to meet someone famous."
"I wish for a grand adventure."
"So it was a magical sword all along! I knew no mortal swordsman could best me in a fair duel!"
"I'll train harder. That's what I'll do! I'll get up at the crack of dawn and retire only when my arms can no longer heft a blade. I will have my honor back!"
"I'll train harder. That's what I'll do! I'll get up at the crack of dawn and retire only when my arms can no longer heft a blade. I will have my honor back!"
"I just don't understand it. That milquetoast should never have defeated me - not in a hundred years! I'm 'the Giddler,' damn it! What an absolute fiasco! I'll never live this down."
"I wonder how much it would cost to hire this Drizzt fellow to tutor me? I should tell daddy to look into it."
"Damn them. *I* should be leading the valiant charge against the shadowy interlopers! Not Bale 'Three pints and I'm done' Khodolis!"

"Bah. He's always been a milksop, too nervous to talk to girls, too nervous even to yell and chastise his servants in the correct manner. Recently, however, he's changed. Ever since he found that sword, he is a new man."

"The Thentian Resistance Army is dedicated to ending the threat of the Shadovar scourge! We are few in number and even less impressive in martial prowess, but one thing we don't lack is refinement! The noble sons and daughters of Thentia shall not be cowed!"

"That fop Khodolis had the temerity to challenge me to a duel for leadership of the Resistance Army - and actually won! It makes no sense. My swordsmanship is nigh legendary around these parts. Until recently, Bale didn't even know how to hold a sword."
"Farewell."
"I hear the Shadovar are searching the nearby ruins."
"What do you know about Bale Khodolis?"
"What can you tell me about this 'Resistance Army?' "
"Why are you so upset?"
"I don't want to talk. I just want to die..."
"An eternity in the Nine Hells is better than being stuck here."
"I've thought about ending it all so many times I've lost count, but I've never found the strength..."
"I haven't seen the sun in days..."
"I should never have ventured so close to human lands."
"The evil of humanity is laid bare here. That such a place can exist is an affront to all that is good."
"If I don't return to the outside world soon, I fear I will wither away."
"Why won't Corellon Larethian hear my pleas?"
"I ain't one for pitying an elf, but this place is grim even by a dwarf's reckoning. The fair folk here be suffering a special form of hell."
"If it weren't for those damned golems, I'd bury me axe in the Innovator's skull!"
"Me body be aching with more bruises than I can count."
"I wish I could bring this whole foul edifice crashing down!"
"Think you're tough? Well, I'm tougher!"
"Only the strong survive in here. You won't make it."
"What you lookin' at?"
"Pray to your god that you never have to fight *me* in the arena!"

The huge shadowy dragon flaps her leathery wings, sending a sickening carnal stench washing over you. She opens her maw, revealing gigantic teeth, razor-sharp and stained with blood. The dragon's voice is a sibilant whisper.

"More of you? The feast grows ever larger! The steel shells of these humans will pose little problem to my fangs and claws - after you have served as the appetizer. Be grateful, for your death will be swift."

The dragon regards you silently for a moment and then snarls softly. "Few have the courage to speak so to the mighty Gloomfang. I should kill you for your insolence, tear your tiny body into small pieces and scatter them to the wind. But you intrigue me."
The dragon grins a terrible, toothy smile. "I prefer my food riper, but you will suffice until I descend on Voonlar and tear the town apart. Die, worm!"

The dragon snorts. "Summoned demons and slaadi. Terrifying creatures for the likes of you, but they know better than to molest me. A balor named Kazz'Temmet leads the demons. The death slaad Grazkahn commands the slaadi. The two groups hate each other."

"I serve no creature! One of the leaders of the group, the wizard Maganus, approached me and proposed an alliance. He has offered me great riches in return for my assistance. Even my contempt for the Crippled Fang - that abomination of dragonkind - could not deter me."

"The fools were in the wrong place at the wrong time. The human Maganus wants every member of the Zhentarim killed on sight. I allowed a few to escape to Voonlar - to spread the panic there before I smash the town to pieces. They will die eventually."
"This is one meal that will choke you to death."
"I fear you underestimate me, dragon."
"I will not listen to your evil words, foul beast!"
"I'm done talking."
"Tell me about the fiends on the road."
"Do you serve the Order of the Crippled Fang?"
"Why did you kill all these Zhentarim?"
"It certainly is cold in the north this time of year."
"If only uncle Jansen could see me now! Rarely has a gnome travelled so far from home."
"I wonder about the nature of this 'Rex' the High Artificer keeps talking about!"
"I've travelled all the way from Lantan to see this place. It's incredible!"
"One day I shall make pilgrimage to the High House of Wonders."
"You are welcome here, of course, but please try not to interfere with the machinery."
"While much can be achieved with magic and prayer, there is no better savior than our own ingenuity."
"The Lord of all Smiths is ever-present in our works here."
"Necessity is the mother of invention."
Floating in the center of the chamber is a beholder of immense size. Its gigantic maw twists into a sneer as its many eyes turn to regard you.
"More puny ones come to serve Gorlax? Or do you seek death? Speak, worm, or I will tear my answers from your worthless mind!"
"Leaving here is no longer an option. Your fate was sealed the moment you discovered my lair."

"You are a fool to have come here. I have lived for centuries. Plotting. Planning. The Zhentarim shall be mine and then the city. Soon all the lands above will tremble before Gorlax the Many-Eyed. Kill them, my minions!"

"Hah! I am neither a wyrm to be flattered nor a typical member of my species to be fooled by insincere flattery. I disgust you, as you disgust me. I care not for your respect. Only your obedience. Only for your servitude."

"I care not for your names, creature. They mean nothing to me. If you refer to the one who first discovered me here, I bent her to my will. She laid the traps that should have stopped you. It seems she failed. I will punish her once I am done with you."

"I am Gorlax the Many-Eyed, most ancient among my kind. They consider me insane, for though my eyes are many, my mind is one. With these umber hulks, I burrowed through the ruins to this cesspit of human filth. Soon I will dominate all in the city above. They will worship me as a god."
"Excuse me. I was just leaving."
"Time for you to die, monster."
"I am here to pay my respects, mighty Gorlax."
"What did you do to Tyana?"
"Who are you?"
"Why do you trouble me, fool?"
"Buorstag is going to slice you in half!"
"Why are you standing around? Help hunt down the rest of those fiends, you fool!"

The great doors of the temple yawn wide before you. Once you step outside, your time in the Moonsea will be over. You pause for a moment and remember all that you have been through. The enemies vanquished. The people you have helped. The friends won and lost.

There is a famous poem by the bard Mintiper Moonsilver. "So high a price, so willingly paid. Hot blood flows, and a ruler is made." Having spent the last few months among some of the worst tyrants in the Realms, you understand this truth better than most.

Yet for every tyrant, there is a hero willing to stand against them. You have defeated a cult, shattered a monstrous army, and banished the vilest of demon lords back to the Abyss. You have earned the right to call yourself the Hero of the Moonsea.

"What a curious series of events. I lose track of who is worse than whom. It seems the Moonsea would be better off if all involved were dead. Still, you proved a valuable ally. I would like to continue traveling with you if you will have me."

"Well, that was a memorable adventure, and I don't say that lightly, seeing as I'm old enough to recall the Fall of Netheril. I still want to get my hands - metaphorically speaking - on Dominion. We make quite the team, so you're welcome to join me."

"The Thar threat has been neutralized. The Zhentarim have been weakened. And a formidable demon lord has been banished back to the Abyss. You're a true hero, <FirstName>. You have my gratitude - for everything."
This death slaad appears larger and stronger than others of his kind.

"No, Grazkahn needs the sword to return home. Refuse, and Grazkahn shall take it by force!"
Grazkahn's eyes shine as he lifts the huge sword from your grasp. "Stand back, mortal, unless you wish to be sucked into the Outer Planes..."

"The one called Kazz'Temmet wields a sword forged in the depths of the Abyss, a powerful blade with strong ties to the Lower Planes. Perhaps if Grazkahn had this sword, he could break the bonds that keep him here."
"Hard to believe, but I sense you speak the truth. What of his sword?"
The eyes of the slaad lord widen as you show him the sword. "Yes... the blade hungers to return to the Abyss. The pull is strong. Give Grazhahn the sword!"

Grazkahn's eyes shine as he lifts the sword from your grasp. "Stand back, mortal, unless you wish to be sucked into the Outer Planes...."
"Perhaps a month as you mortals count the passing of time. Grazkahn already tires of this mortal plane."
"His name? Maganus - the one-eyed raven mage. Grazkahn would love to devour his flesh. Too great is his power though. Not worth the risk."
Grazkahn throws his head back and laughs, a foul gurgling that reverberates around the hills. "The balor? A coward, that one, sending mortals to do his work. What is your name?"
"Be grateful we have recently eaten. Leave quickly unless you wish to offer up your tender flesh."
"Are you so desperate to die? Demons, devils, even dragons - all have sought to defeat the great Grazkahn. All have died. Now a <race> would seek to slay me at the behest of a balor. Why?"

"Are you ready to face your next opponents? The crowd is baying for your blood."

"What is this? Has the old fool used his healing powers on you? No matter. I have a special surprise for you, <FirstName>. You are to witness the long overdue death of the mage Blizzard."

"After, you will step into the pit once more and defend yourself against the ogres that assaulted Father Garth. They were not brutal enough with the old man; their punishment shall be death at your hands!"
"There is little time to waste. You do not want to be late for the execution..."
"That's what I like to hear."

"Were you a less valuable prisoner, I'd have my golems pluck off your limbs and feed them to the beasts in their cells while you watch. But you're worth more to me than that. Your suffering here shall be... legendary."

"I will not pretend I am not upset about the magic golem. You were not supposed to survive that encounter. Still, your popularity with the patrons has increased immeasurably. Your ruthless execution of the wizard was a delight to behold."

"Indeed, I have received news that Lord Maalthiir himself will attend your next fight. For this, I have something special planned. An ex-champion of the Arena, no less. A monster so vicious many have hanged themselves in their cells rather than die a bloody death at his hands."

"I once pitted the Red Minotaur against three fire giants. I was sure he could not defeat the trio - not all at once. They were larger and perhaps slightly stronger - and there were three of them and only one of him."

"He stacked their remains in a neat pile and then climbed it so that his eyes were level with those of Lord Maalthiir. This act won him his freedom. Maalthiir admires ruthlessness and courage above all else."
"Though I would love to throw your aching body against the beast and see how you fare, Lord Maalthiir must be given the best show possible. Rest and recover your strength. Then come speak with me."

"The Red Minotaur - the only gladiator ever to be granted his freedom by Lord Maalthiir. The memory of his opponents spraying red gore, their innards hanging from the beast's horns, is one that I shall forever treasure."

"Those two are of no concern to you! They are weak, pathetic fools and thus not fit to share a cell with one seeking to gain favor with Lord Maalthiir. You need no distractions while you prepare for your next fight."
While you can't see the expression behind the mask, you can hear the fury in the arena master's voice. His anger is ferocious.
"You fool! My fight announcer gave you the opportunity to impress the crowd with an act that would have instantly made you their favorite - and you spurned it!"

"Still, your actions have sent a wave of gossip rippling through the city. Lord Maalthiir himself has sent me news that he is to attend your next fight. I am pleased to say it is one you will not survive - not against my ex-champion."
With an audible sigh, the arena master waves his hands. The golems guarding the gates suddenly hum to life and stride towards you.
"Lord Maalthiir has just arrived, and the crowd is working itself into a frenzy. This is going to be the greatest spectacle the Arena has ever seen!"
"Before you step into the pit, make sure you speak with Drizzle the Alchemist. I want you fully prepared for this fight. Lord Maalthiir must not be disappointed."

"The stage is set! The Red Minotaur is as vicious as I remember him. Why, I just threw half-a-dozen gladiators against him, and he tore through them in minutes. If you hurry up, you might catch him finishing off the last two. He he he!"
"Now go. Entertain Lord Maalthiir."

The two massive constructs tower over you - and some strange force pins your arms to your sides. Try as you might, you can't attack the arena master. He chuckles horribly. "With a word, I could have you killed. That is the power I have over you, <FirstName>."

"An acquaintance of mine placed a Geas upon you before having you delivered here. I believe you know him: Wak Rathar. Until the spell is removed, you are incapable of harming me. Isn't that fortunate?"
"Now that we've established the futility of your situation, let us move on to more important matters."
"That's what they all say. Let me assure you; death is the only way out of here."
"What have you done to me?"
"You sicken me."
"Save the petty villainy. I won't be here long."
"What do you mean 'break me'?"
<StartAction>[Remain silent.]</Start>
<StartAction>[Remain silent.]</Start>
<StartAction>[Remain silent.]</Start>
<StartAction>[Leave.]</Start>
"I can handle a couple of rusty golems."
"How about I cut you down instead?"
<StartAction>[Remain silent.]</Start>
"Release me, or your death will be ten times as painful as I had planned."
"What have you done to me?"
"I'm going to tear you limb from limb."
"Free potions, eh? Sounds good to me."
"Who is this alchemist?"
"Bah! There's little that can threaten me."
"I won't fight for your amusement!"
"Hang on. I need a moment or two."
"I'm ready."
"What now?"
"Bring it on! I'll butcher whatever you place before me!"
"I hope my next opponent is more challenging."
"What have you done with Father Garth?"
<StartAction>[Remain silent.]</Start>
"Give me another minute."
"I'm ready."
"Hold on one moment."
"I'm ready."
"I fear nothing."
"You think I fear your golems? I'll smash them to pieces!"
"Say what you will; he'll die by my hands."
"Who is this ex-champion?"
"Where are Elf and Father Garth?"
<StartAction>[Remain silent.]</Start>
"Release me, or your death will be ten times as painful as I had planned."
"So, you couldn't resist taking the bait. Thanks to you, I have been relieved of my position in the Arena. At least I had my fun with Onehand - he refused to scream. I doubt you'll prove as tough."
"Blustering idiot! Your ego is as sickening as Father Garth's piety! Lest you forget, Wak Rathar's Geas prohibits you from causing me the slightest harm."

"Your arrogance is amusing. Before I was given command of the Arena, *I* was the greatest gladiator that Hillsfar had ever seen! Lest you forget, Wak Rathar's Geas prohibits you from causing me the slightest harm."
"Ah, always the valiant fool. This time I'm going to take matters into my own hands. Lest you forget, Wak Rathar's Geas prohibits you from causing me the slightest harm."

"As always, Wak's scheming was impeccable. Your presence here has robbed you of the protection Lord Maalthiir's order afforded you. All that remains is for me to flay the very flesh from your bones! Die, fool!"
"I don't listen to the words of dead men."
"You dare to threaten me even after witnessing my prowess?"
"I'll put a stop to your evil here and now."
"This is wonderful, just wonderful. Wootabega!"
"I gauge your chances of having achieved success to be fifty-fifty."

"The great Ikathilo of Lantan spent many years in this temple, researching the creation of golems and their application. None, not even Hlessen Muragh, were his equal in this field. Alas, he passed away some time ago. Unfortunately, he left his notes where none could reach."

"You see, such was Ikathilo's dedication to his craft that he setup a workshop in Mechanus itself, in the Outer Planes. The portal to his workshop can be found in his chambers. However, the High Artificer had this area of the temple closed."

"Ikathilo was ultimately slain by his own creations. He made it back to the temple before he died, thankfully, and received a burial befitting one of Gond's greatest servants. Still, his errant golems yet remain in his workshop, along with his notes. Their value is incalculable."
"A simple deduction! I do indeed. You may keep whatever else of value you find in his workshop. Just, please return anything you find concerning golem creation."

"On the contrary, I suspect he would secretly be thrilled! As head of the temple, he cannot be seen to risk the lives of Gond's faithful. You, on the other hand... I dare say this plan has his blessing, even if he would never admit it."
"That... is most unexpected. Have I miscalculated? Excuse me, I need to figure out what went wrong."

"I was seventy-five per cent certain you would say that! Ikathilo's room is in the basement, in the very bottom of the complex. If I recall, his golems were highly resistant to slashing and piercing weapons, so I would suggest you 'get your bash on.'"
"Remember, it is Ikathilo's notes concerning the creation of golems that I require. Whatever else his workshop holds is yours to be plundered."

"My name is Isaac Glinkle, of Lantan. I am what you might call a mathmagician. Did you know that everything you see and hear can be explained by mathematics? There is a pattern to reality, discernible to those who possess the key."

The gnome extends a long finger and taps himself on the side of the head. "Education. Wisdom is only possessed by the learned. The monks of Candlekeep are wrong about many things, but on this matter, they are quite correct."

"Yes... Yes, this is the seminal masterwork from which most of our understanding of advanced golem creation springs! Ikathilo might be gone, but his knowledge will live on in perpetuity! You have my gratitude, hero! Please accept this with my deepest thanks."
"Just as I predicted."
This wizened gnome examines you with intense interest, subjecting you to the kind of scrutiny a horse trader might give to a promising young stallion.
"Hmm... Yes... Yes, I think you'll do nicely. According to my mathematics, you are, I would say, somewhat north of fifteen. Perhaps twenty? Well up to the task, I should imagine."
"Farewell for now. You'll be back, I am almost one hundred per cent certain of that."

"Patterns, dear <boy/girl>. They are everywhere. The immutable laws of the multiverse enforce them on all things eventually. I note your fine gear, your confident stride. I can say with some accuracy that you are in the very highest percentile of <race>s."

"That's because you live with your head in the clouds, metaphorically speaking! Too much magic rots the brain. The kind of magic I wield, that of mathematics, is accessible to all who apply themselves."

"The point is this: I require a truly extraordinary individual for a task I suspect will prove extremely dangerous. Fatally so? Perhaps. The rewards, however, are great. I can predict this with near certainty. Allow me to elaborate."
"I have 'The Art of Golem Crafting' right here."
"Go on."
"Why would he do that?"
"You want me to retrieve these notes."
"The High Artificer would not be pleased."
"I think I'll pass."
"I'll do it."
"I've decided I'll retrieve the notes."
"Who are you?"
"What is the key?"
"What were you talking about again?"
"Farewell."
"What are you talking about?"
"Can you get to the point?"
"I still don't understand."

A strong acrid scent assails you as you enter the vast cavern. Somewhere on the far side of the chamber, you hear something huge shift - and then a deep chuckle. A mighty voice echoes through the cavern, as sinister as infanticide.
"YOU DARE ENTER THE LAIR OF IYRAUROTH, WYRM OF THE PEAKS? SLAYER OF OLOGH, TERROR OF GLISTIG, MIGHTIEST WYRM OF THE VAST, AND FUTURE KING OF THIS LAND OF MEN?"

"IMPUDENT FOOLS! I WAS OLD WHEN THAR WAS FOUNDED! WHEN THE THARKUL INVADES, I SHALL SWOOP DOWN AND TEAR YOUR CITIES ASUNDER! FOR NOW, MY CHILDREN SHALL FEAST ON YOUR FLESH. KILL THEM. KILL THEM ALL. DEATH! DEATH!"
"Well met again. Will you hear my plea?"

"There are several sewer grates dotted around the city. They all lead to a maze of sewers below. They are dangerous, no place for a lone thief with limited combat skill. But you could survive down there and perhaps learn the cause of Tyana's madness."
"The guild has coin, or at least it once did, as well as other resources. If you help uncover what is wrong with Tyana Softfoot, I am certain she would reward you generously."
"I will wait here and keep an eye on Sparrow. Return to me if you learn anything."
"Thank you again for your help. You have saved the guild."
"Worry not for Sparrow. I will look after her."
"Nope. Goodbye."
"Go on."
"Hardly a compelling case to risk my life."
"Very well. I'll look into it."

The two young women in the cell before you are filthy and look half starved. The resemblance is obvious enough for you to know straightaway that they are sisters. From the dark shadows under their eyes, it appears they haven't slept much.
"Sister! Sister, wake up! Someone is here!"
"Please find the key to our cell! One of the jailers has it. He should be somewhere close."

"Oh, thank you! Any longer in this horrible place and I don't think we would have survived. If you ever have cause to visit the Temple of the Moon in Thentia, I'm sure our mistress, Sureene, would reward you."
"May Mystra guide you. Come, sister. Let's get out of here."

"I am so sorry, but neither my sister nor I are in any condition to fight. Our magic was depleted long ago. I perhaps have a spell or two left in case we stumble across any orcs. But we would be no use against a mage like Maganus."

"He is performing a great summoning ritual with the oni - the eldest and most powerful of the ogre mages who call Thar home. Kragdar was simply their pawn, a figurehead to unite the humanoids of Thar. They wish great ill on the Moonsea."
"Thank you again for rescuing us."
"May Mystra guide you. Come, sister. Let's get out of here."
"Uh... Please... no more... You've hurt us enough..."
"Tell me, stranger, why are you here? Do you serve Maganus, or have you come to free us?"
"Please don't abandon us! I fear what the orcs will do next time they return."
"One of the orc jailers has the key to our cell. If you free us, we can make our way back to the House of the Moon in Thentia."
"Maganus placed us in this cell. He has not mistreated us, but the same cannot be said of the orcs and other humanoids who are marshaled here. I fear my sister has suffered worse than I."

"I am Jannatha. This is my younger sister, Baerimel. We are both wizards. We came here to investigate the increased activity around the citadel. We didn't expect a powerful archmage would be here. He discovered us and took us prisoner."
"I don't think these are with the ogres, Bae. They're not orcs. At least, most of them aren't."
"Fair lady, what do you mean by 'most'? I see no orcs-- Oh. I see. You meant me."
"I'll return soon."
"You mentioned Maganus."
"Tell me again how you got here."
"Farewell and good luck."
"Your mistress had better reward me."
"You said you are wizards. Can you help me fight Maganus?"
"Do you know what Maganus is planning?"
"I'll just leave you here a moment."
"I'll free you. Tell me how."
"I seek Maganus, but I do not serve him."
"Who are you? How did you get here?"

This hulking frost giant must be near sixteen feet tall. His long snowy beard is plaited with small bones, likely of human origin. He grunts and shifts his weight as you approach, readying himself for a strike with his fearsome battleaxe.

"Who are ye that dares invade the lair of the mighty Bashnagg, Jarl of the great Bloodaxe tribe of Thar? At least there be more meat on yer bones than the old woman - Agatha can toss yer remains in the stewpot once I've finished tearing ye limb from limb!"
"Har har, but I do like it when ye small folk have some spirit in ye. Makes it all the more entertaining when I'm plucking yer limbs off one at a time. Prepare to meet yer doom!"
"Aye, is that what ye think? Yonder dragon was a fearsome one, I'll grant ye, until I tamed it with the edge o' me axe!"

"Why'd I want to talk with the likes of ye for? Aye, I know what yer thinking: 'He's a big bloody giant, doesn't have two brain cells to rub together.' The last o' the little folk that tried any tongue trickery on me ended up spread all over the ground."
"Not that it's any o' yer business, but the ogres of Kur-Tharsu be massing once more under their new Tharkul, and I've no desire to bend me knee to an ogre king."
"Amberlyn? That's the wrinkly old hag, aye? Ye'll be joining 'er shortly in old Agatha's cook pot. It's been a while since I had meself a good bit o' <race> meat."
"Stupid oaf! Prepare to meet your death!"
"Look around, giant. Your minions couldn't stop me."
"There's no need for violence."
"What are you giants doing so far from Thar?"
"What have you done with Amberlyn?"
The skeleton says nothing. It is a mindless undead minion once again.
Standing before you is a skeleton. Much to your astonishment, it speaks in a voice that sounds very human - and very surprised.
"How did YOU get in here? Only the dead can gain entrance to this place!"
"Guilty as charged. I know you - not the voice, but the words. The rhythm, the cadence. Dragoth... ?"
"LYRESSA? Can it be? You're alive! I mean, you're... you. My Lyressa."
"I am not your Lyressa. I... I don't know what I am. I want answers, Dragoth. I want to know what you did to me."
"I will give you the answers you seek. I promise. Meet me in my study. There we shall talk."
"I have a bad feeling about this. I've wanted answers for so long, but now that I'm so close... I'm scared what I will discover."
"I'm glad to have you beside me at least. Come on. Dragoth is waiting in his study."
"Let's just hurry this up."
"Better to see the truth than live a lie."
"I'm here for you, Lyressa."
"The Bron is absolutely fuming. Whoever he picked a fight with beat him up pretty bad."

Standing before the corpses of Craster and his elven companions is their killer - the draconic warrior you encountered briefly back at the Order encampment. He leans casually on his huge greatsword, a weapon that seems to hum with power.

"Three soft-skins, and none of them put a scratch on me. The big one might have been dangerous were he not as slow as an ox. This is why your kind is but vermin compared with the glory of dragonkind. You are weak creatures, unfit to rule a land such as this."

"His whereabouts should not concern you! Your 'victory' back in our camp was meaningless. You have depleted our numbers, but the Order will reform as quickly as my mother's undead body. That is the power this sword possesses. That - and the power to deal swift death!"

The half-dragon laughs, a rasping sound. "To sow death and destruction. To see this wretched human land tear itself apart. Maganus desires only to see the Zhentarim dead. I would see ALL of humanity wiped out. For the time being, our goals match."

The half dragon snorts in amusement. "My mother will reform in time. She is incredibly difficult to destroy. That alone has proven true among the lies spewed by the conniving worms of the Cult of the Dragon."
"They may call themselves that, but to associate those lying maggots with the greatest beings on the planet is an insult to dragonkind."
"You are cold. Cold and efficient. Those qualities I admire, even when possessed by one as inherently weak as yourself."
"You think I ran in fear? I could see you were occupied. I did not wish to ruin the prospect of a fair duel by intervening. These three were but a diversion to pass the time until you arrived."

"They would have killed me had they the strength. Killed me or attempted to subjugate me and make me their slave. But they were weak. Thus, they died. Strength is ever the ultimate virtue. The last and truest argument."

"My mother was foolish to trust the lies of the soft-skins. You saw what has become of her. Once she was known as Shashurra the Red Death, scourge of the Moonsea. Now she is simply the Crippled Fang. A sad name for a sad creature."

The half-dragon's harsh voice grows angry. "Human magelings tricked her into accepting their false promises of immortality. When I saw what they had done to my mother, I slew them all. Then I swore vengeance upon all the soft-skins."

"They were mere slaves, bound to my mother's will through the power of this sword. It is Netherese in origin, a gift from the archmage Maganus to seal our alliance. He is a soft-skin I can respect. His wrath exceeds even my own."
"You think you can challenge ME? Karandas of the blood of Shashurra, First Sword of the Fang and future heir to the southern Moonsea? Your hubris is amusing. Prepare to die, fool!"

"Your only contact with this sword shall be of the swift and fatal sort! It holds power beyond your comprehension. With it, a mortal could enslave the minds of dozens. In my mother's claws, an army shall be raised."
"That's some tidy work there."
"I could use a sword like that."
"Where is this Maganus?"
"Tell me about this alliance."
"You fled earlier and allowed her to die."
<StartAction>[Insight]</Start> "That sounds like the work of the Cult of the Dragon."
"You've found some courage since the last time we met."
"Murderer! Why did you kill these innocent people?"
"That didn't stop you working with human cultists."
"Let's end this."

This huge bear of a man smells of the wilds. His voice is deep and booming. "Ah, I did not realize guests were free to wander wherever they pleased! No matter. A new friend is always welcome! I am Karim Ninetrees. A pleasure to meet you."
"A pleasure. You'll have to join me for a drink sometime!"
"I'll say a quick prayer to Silvanus for its soul. Now, where's my knife..."
Karim quickly cuts his palm and bleeds over the pelt, marking it with his scent. "There. That ought to do it. Now, I had better leave in case those Malarites don't buy your story. My thanks again."
<< Default Dialog >>
"Farewell."
<< Special Dialog >>
"Can't a man enjoy a rest after weeks in the wild? I'm a ranger, a forest guide to folk who need one. I also look after the local animals and keep the wilderness free of scum from Thar."
Karim immediately bristles, his face quickly turning red. "Can't say I do. Besides, werebears are only vicious when riled. What do you want with this werebear anyway?"
"Fine. Maybe you ought to leave me be."

"You're WHAT?! Those murderous trophy hunters? If it's a werebear you're after, you've found him - but then you knew that, didn't you? I ain't never killed an innocent, but the Malarites themselves beget evil lycanthropes that DO!"

"I don't know your character, stranger, but if you value what's right, you'll tell the Malarites to shove it. Better yet, bring me a bear pelt - any pelt will do - and I'll stain it with my blood. You can say it's mine and claim your reward."
"You're welcome to try - but you'll find that Karim Ninetrees won't go down without a fight! Rargh!"
"Can't say I enjoy the thought of an innocent bear having its pelt taken, but it'll bring a smile to my face to put one over on those savages."
"Hello again! How can I help?
"Farewell."
"Deal. I'll return with a bear pelt."
"I've decided just to kill you."
"I have the bear pelt."
"What are you doing here?"
"I'm looking for a vicious werebear. Have any leads?"
"Mind your business."
"I'm hunting it for the faithful of Malar."
"I'd rather just kill you."
This towering balor carries a serrated greatsword forged from some dark metal. He watches you approach but makes no move to attack. The smell of fire and brimstone is overpowering.
The demon's voice is harsh and filled with depthless evil. "Greetings, mortal. I am Kazz'Temmet, Lord of the Infernal Pit and Master of the Twelve Blades of Gorgos. Hear my words."

The balor's horrid mouth curves upward in a grin. "You have done well, mortal. Few have the power to defeat such a being. As your reward, I shall grant you a swift death. Don't look so surprised; powerful souls such as yours are of great value in the Blood War."
The balor hisses. "Yes? What did the overgrown toad say?"

The balor's fanged mouth twists in anger. "Insolent worm! You dare suggest I part with this sword? I shall cleave you in half and then unleash the fury of the Abyss upon Grazkahn and his wretched slaadi!"
"You return. Tell me you will slay the slaad lord, Grazkahn."
"You return. What of the slaad lord? Do not disappoint me, mortal."
"Hurry, mortal. Every moment you linger allows Grazkahn time to summon more of his kind."

The balor's horrid mouth curves upward in a grin. "You have done well, mortal. Few have the power to defeat such a being. As your reward, I shall grant you a swift death. Don't look so surprised; powerful souls such as yours are of great value in the Blood War."

The balor's fanged mouth twists in anger. "Insolent worm! You dare suggest I part with this sword? I shall cleave you in half and then unleash the fury of the Abyss upon Grazkahn and his wretched slaadi!"

"Foolish mortal! You dare defy the Lord of the Infernal Pit? I offered you a chance to do me a great service and walk away with your life. You have doomed your worthless soul to an eternity of damnation!"
The balor's eyes narrow on you. "Return when you wish to hear of riches and power beyond your imagining."
For a moment, the balor's terrible skull-like visage twists in rage, and the fire shrouding his giant form burns brighter. "I offered you civility, mortal. I expect the same - if you wish to live."
"My demons have doubtless tested you already - and failed. Rather than kill you, I would offer you an opportunity."

"The wizard that summoned me also brought a slaad lord by the name of Grazkahn into this mortal realm. Grazkahn has since summoned others of his kin, the vanguard of an army. Their presence is inconvenient to my plans."

"I want you to slay Grazkahn. I would deal with him myself but for the fact I must remain here and keep my demons under control. If they are left free to roam, they will draw the attention of powerful mages to the south. I am not ready for that. Not yet."

"If you do this, I will reward you with riches far greater than you ever dreamed of. What is there to lose? You remove a threat to these lands and gain wealth beyond that of most kings. What say you, mortal?"
"Good. Grazkahn is east of here near the city you mortals call Hillsfar. Return when he is dead."

"Foolish mortal! You dare defy the Lord of the Infernal Pit? I offered you a chance to do me a great service and walk away with your life. You have doomed your worthless soul to an eternity of damnation!"
"I must go."
"What's in it for me if I slay this slaad lord?"
"I refuse to help you."
"I will do it."
"I would never help a demon, no matter the circumstances."
"He's already dead. I killed him."
"I have already spoken with Grazkahn."
"He needs your sword in order to leave this plane."
"There's little chance of that, fiend."
"Why should I listen to you, fiend?"
"I have not yet made any progress."
"Grazkahn is dead."
"He needs your sword in order to leave this plane."
"Evidently my power has you cowering like a worm."
"Why haven't you attacked me?"
"I'm listening."
"I need time to think on this."
"I think I'd rather kill you."
"Avast there, mate. What can Kettia and the crew of the Voyager do for you?"
"Well met again. I can feel the vast lake calling to me. I long to ride her once more."
"Aye. Return when you're ready to depart."
"Aye. When would you like to go?"
"I will not have those filthy beasts aboard my ship! Dismount your horses and return to me when you are prepared to travel."
"Those Marels had no business attacking my ship."
"Curse that man! His arrogance is everything that is wrong with Melvaunt. Arrogance and prejudice and not a damn to give for anyone not of noble blood. He spoke of slaves as cargo, not as people."
"I... don't quite understand your humor, <FirstName>. Never mind. We will speak of this no more."

"I recall hearing a rumor that Veris of the Purple Star likes to lay low in Mulmaster. He is a cruel and violent man. I would shed no tears at his death, even in the service of a man like the Lord of Waves."
"Let us set sail for our destination. Weigh anchor, me hearties!"

"You are not at fault. Attitudes in the Moonsea are not as enlightened as in other parts of the Realms. Unfortunately, Thay and Calimshan, two of the most powerful nations, still rely on the blood of slaves."
"The Admiral wishes to speak with us. Follow me."
This tall, confident woman has a patchwork of scars on her dark face. She smiles at you, revealing white teeth, a good number of which are capped with gold.
"That was close. I've ordered my crew to fix the damage and drain the water. Let's avoid this stretch of the Moonsea in the future - I've no wish to die just yet..."
"Quickly! Destroy the elementals so that my crew can repair the damage, or else the Moonsea will become our grave!"
"<FirstName>, water elementals have broken through the hull! Get below decks and fight them off before the Voyager capsizes!"
"That Burak was a nasty fellow. I will shed no tears at his passing. Shall we be off, then?"
"Don't look at me! Fight the pirates!"
"We have been boarded by pirates! Best see what they want."

"<FirstName>! There's a huge blockade ahead of us, pirate ships each and every one! It's as if every pirate in the Moonsea has sailed to Zhentil Keep. We'll never get through. Not without a navy to break the blockade."

"There's something big happening in the Keep too - you see the smoke there? The city is burning. I saw men and women throw themselves into the harbor and drown rather than face whatever has been unleashed."

"If anyone can convince Mulmaster to send aid, it's you. The Moonsea hasn't seen a hero with more influence in decades, if ever. Maybe the High Blade will even grant you a personal audience. I'll order the crew to set sail on your say-so."
"Not unless you can somehow teleport everyone into Zhentil Keep - but there's bad magic there, so I wouldn't recommend it. You'd probably end up inside out."
"Well, hello. My name is Kettia Freeborn, and I am the captain of the Grim Voyager. She's a small ship, but true, and my crew are the best bunch a woman could find."

"Zhentil Keep doesn't have many friends in the Moonsea. The only city with a navy that might be willing to help is Mulmaster. Every other city would gladly see Zhentil Keep burn. Which seems to be what is happening."
"I wish I knew. There must be upwards of twenty ships. There hasn't been a pirate fleet this large since the time of Avagard the Black..."
"Avagard the Black. He was a legendary pirate king. Disappeared decades ago, though, so this can't be him - surely. I mean, if he's still alive, he'd be well into his eighties. Why return now?"
"Only Mulmaster's navy can break this blockade."
